newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Maastricht sees slight fall in air freight in '96.
newsitem.headline: Maastricht sees slight fall in air freight in '96.

text.p: Maastricht Aachen Airport (MAA) has seen a slight decrease in freight volumes in 1996, an airport statement said.
Freight volumes totalled around 46,952 tonnes last year if trucked airfreight was also included. The total was slightly down on 1995, when total volumes were 48,355 tonnes.
The MAA was also still in the red in 1996 but its loss did decline by 30 percent to 3.6 million guilders ($1.9 million) for the year.

Charter freight dropped by nine percent to 12,250 tonnes from 13,500 in 1995 as a result of the southern Dutch airport's policy to ban Russian Ilyushin 76 aircraft following residential complaints. The last IL-76 used the airport late last year.
MAA said a sharp drop in European volumes - both charter and scheduled - was compensated for by a strong rise in scheduled intercontinental freight traffic.

There had also been a decrease in trucked airfreight volumes to 4,517 tonnes from 13,325 tonnes in 1995 following the final closure early this year of British Airways trucking hub in Maastricht, the airport said in its 1996 annual.
This year, the MAA expects a steady growth in scheduled freight volumes but it is expecting a severe drop in charter activities.
As well as the IL-76 ban, the Dutch government has restricted Maastricht's night flights to 950 a year.
Landing fee revenues increased by 14 percent to 6.1 million guilders and handling fees increased by five percent to 8.5 million guilders in 1996.
Turnover at the Dutch airport increased by 16.9 percent to 18.4 million guilders from 16.9 million.
